title: Binary Contracts, Protobuf & Schema Evolution
subtitle: Tag-numbered wire compatibility, Schema Registry gates & poison-pill DLQs
overview: In continuous rolling deployments across dozens of microservices, old and new versions of producers and consumers run side by side simultaneously. Schema evolution via binary field tags (Protobuf/Thrift) and Schema Registries (Avro) keeps rolling releases 100% zero-downtime without breaking upstream callers or consumers.
firstPrinciplesStory: You ship Billing Service v2.1 adding one new required JSON field `tax_jurisdiction`. Halfway through the rolling deploy, v2.0 pods reject v2.1 events with HTTP 400 while older consumers crash trying to parse fields they didn't expect—cascading across Kafka into 100k stuck invoices. Binary schema tags paired with strict forward/backward compatibility rules prevent rolling schema breaks at CI build time.

adaptiveLenses.intuition: Imagine sending packages with numbered slot stickers instead of long English labels: if slot #14 appears on a form printed next week, an older clerk simply skips slot #14 cleanly while still processing slots #1–#13—never throwing away the envelope.
adaptiveLenses.mechanics: Protobuf/Thrift encode integers (`tag = 1, 2, 14`) rather than string field names, saving 3–7x payload size. Avro omits tags per record and embeds a 5-byte Schema Registry ID header. Both require never reusing deleted tag numbers and adding new fields strictly as `optional` with safe defaults via Expand-Contract deploys.
adaptiveLenses.staffTradeoffs: Adopt TPP Design by Contract: fail breaking wire changes cleanly in CI (`FULL_TRANSITIVE` compatibility checks) rather than discovering schema breaks in production. Wrap Kafka deserializers with a monitored Dead-Letter Queue (`billing.dlq`) so corrupted external payloads quarantine safely instead of starving an entire consumer partition, and park the record's key when per-key order matters so later events for it wait behind it.

ddiaAnchors.concept: Forward & Backward Compatibility Across Rolling Deployments
ddiaAnchors.whyItMatters: Guarantees that old writers never break new readers and new writers never break old readers during continuous microservices rollouts.

pragmaticTips.principle: TPP Topic 23 & 28 · Design by Contract & Decoupling
pragmaticTips.tip: Explicitly enforce preconditions/postconditions at service boundaries and keep edge date-versioned JSON adapters decoupled from canonical internal binary schemas.
pragmaticTips.application: Translate legacy v1 JSON requests at the API gateway while keeping core services on cleanly versioned `.proto` contracts.

keyTakeaways: NEVER reuse retired Protobuf/Thrift tag numbers or narrow field numeric types (`int64` -> `int32`).
Binary encoding (Protobuf / Avro) eliminates JSON key bloat and cuts internal RPC bandwidth by ~70%.
Quarantine unparseable poison-pill events into a monitored DLQ rather than crash-looping a partition; when per-key order matters, park the key so its later events wait too.

steps.info: Producer v2.1 registers optional `tax_jurisdiction` (tag `14`); Registry issues cached `schema_id = 42` after `FULL_TRANSITIVE` check.
steps.payloadInspector:
Check: FULL_TRANSITIVE PASS
new optional string tax_jurisdiction = 14
tag_reuse: false | schema_id: 42
steps.inspectorNote: Catching incompatible schema edits at CI build/register time guarantees older running pods will never crash on unknown fields.

steps.info: Writes `0x00 + schema_id=42 + varint tags [1, 2, 14]` cleanly in 310 B instead of 1.3 KB JSON.
steps.inspectorNote: Compact wire tags eliminate repeated JSON property strings and cut cross-AZ replication bandwidth by >70%.

steps.phaseTitle: Forward-Compatible Read on Older Consumer v2.0
steps.info: Tax Consumer v2.0 (only knows tags `1..13`) cleanly skips unknown length-delimited tag `14` and computes tax.
steps.payloadInspector:
Decode v2.0: read tag 1, tag 2
skip unknown tag 14 (wire_type=2, len=5)
result: 200 OK (Zero downtime!)
steps.inspectorNote: Forward compatibility lets teams ship producer v2.1 hours or days before upgrading all consumer deployments.

predictPrompt.prompt: If Tax Consumer v2.0 decodes the v2.1 message, copies tags 1..13 into its own domain struct, and then emits a derived event serialized from that struct, what subtle bug occurs?
predictPrompt.hint: Where would unknown tag #14 live once the data has left the generated Protobuf message?
predictPrompt.reveal: Tag #14 is dropped downstream. Version note: proto2, and proto3 since protobuf 3.5, keep unknown fields when you decode and re-encode the same message type (proto3 3.0–3.4 discarded them). Today the bug appears mainly when you map the message into your own struct or DTO, or convert through JSON, which has no slot for unknown tags.

chaosScenarios.title: Poison-Pill Corrupted Payload Injection
chaosScenarios.triggerSummary: External webhook gateway bypasses CI validation and produces corrupted bytes onto `billing.events` partition 3.
chaosScenarios.mitigationSummary: Consumer deserializes inside a contract try-catch boundary, isolates the malformed record + metadata to `billing.dlq`, parks its invoice_id so later events for that invoice wait behind it, and commits the partition 3 offset.

steps.info: Invalid wire type 7 encountered in offset #90821; consumer contract assertion catches invalid protobuf header.
steps.payloadInspector:
Error: InvalidWireTypeException at offset 90821
Action: Quarantine to DLQ (Do NOT crash-loop pod!)
steps.inspectorNote: Without a DLQ isolation boundary, restarting consumer pods repeatedly re-read offset #90821 and block 100k valid invoices.

steps.info: Quarantines bad frame + `trace_id` to `billing.dlq`, parks its invoice_id, commits offset `90822`, and alerts owners.
steps.payloadInspector:
Topic: billing.dlq
source_partition: 3 | offset: 90821
reason: SchemaDeserializationError
steps.inspectorNote: Decouples one malformed event from healthy stream throughput while preserving forensic evidence. Because the stream is keyed by invoice, later events for the parked invoice are diverted too, so they never apply out of order.

pros: Built-in unknown tag skipping for forward compatibility
Strong IDL code generation across Go/Rust/Python/Java
cons: Tag numbers permanently retired upon deletion
tradeoffs.bestFor: Microservice gRPC meshes and cross-team internal contracts.

pros: Smallest possible Kafka payload (no per-field tags in body)
Self-describing Schema ID header works great for columnar data lakes
cons: Consumers must cache/resolve writer schemas via Schema Registry
tradeoffs.bestFor: High-throughput Kafka event topics and Iceberg/Parquet archival pipelines.
